lawyer:
M Shamsul Alam, DAG with AKM Zahirul Haque, Advocate ----- For the State.
Joynal Abedin and Abdul Malek Sardar, ----- Contemners (appeared in person).
parties:
State ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Joynal Abedin and another ----- Other Party
full_judgment:
Abdul Bari Sarker J: This Rule was issued on the basis of Memo No. 428 dated 6.12.78 of the Court of District Judge, Jhalakati, By the above name, the District Judge, Jhalakati recommended for drawing up contempt proceeding against the condemners Joynal Abedin and Abdul Malek Sardar for making contemptuous allegations against Abul Bashar Munshi, Munsif Nalchiti. Contemner No. 1 Joynal Abedin filed four petitions under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure for transfer of 4 title suits from the Court of Munsif, Nalchiti to any other Court on various allegations and apprehension that the petitioner would not get justice from the Court of the learned Munsif. Applications for transfer of the above suit were numbered as Miscellaneous Nos. 25-28 of 1985 of the Court of District Judge, Jhalakati. The Rule was issued on 1.8.89 in the following terms: 

 "Let a Rule issue calling upon Md. Joynal Abedin, son of late Mofizuddin of village-Chhoto Promoh, Upazila Nalchity, District Jhalakati and Abdul Malek Sardar, son of late Tasimuddin Sarder of village Pronab, Upazila Nalchity, District-Jhalakati to show cause why they shall not be committed for contempt of Court for making wild, false, baseless and contemptuous allegations against the learned Munsif, Nalchity Upazila, District Jhalakati in the application for transfer under section 24 CPC in Miscellaneous Case No. 25/85, 26/85 27/85 and 28/85 in the court of District Judge, Jhalakati thereby scandalising the Court and bringing the Court into disrepute. 

 The circumstances under which the contempt was committed has been described by Mr. Hamidul Haque, District and Sessions Judge, Jhalakati by his judgment and order dated 18.11.86 passed in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case (copy enclosed) which will form the ground of allegations." 

 2. From the above order of this court; it appears that the contemners are asked to show cause on the basis of the alleged contemptuous statements made by them in the four applications filed for transfer filed in the above miscellaneous cases. 

 3. It may be pointed out that contemner No. 2 was not a party to the applications under section 24 CPC in the above miscellaneous cases although, he deposed in them as PW 2. So contemner No. 2 Abdul Malek Sardar cannot be made liable for contempt on the basis of the statements made in those applications. 

 4. Now let us see what contemptuous statements, if any, were made by contemner No. 1 in the applications filed in Court under section 24 CPC which formed the basis of the above miscellaneous cases. In this connection, we like to quote in toto the contents of one of the 4 applications which are more or less similar. In the application filed in Miscellaneous Cause No. 25 of 1985, it is stated as follows: 

 7. From the above words it seems that the opposite party allegedly tried to influence the Munsif through his relations. The allegation is thus clearly against the opposite parties and not against the learned Munsif. Mr. M Shamsul Alam, the learned DAG, submits that the other statements made in the above application do not come within the purview of contempt laws. It may be pointed out that "wild, false and baseless" allegations made in the petition under section 24 CPC do not come within the purview of contempt, if by those statements, no attempt is made to put the Court in disrepute or to discredit it in the eye of others although such allegations may come within the mischief of any other law for taking actions. The learned Deputy Attorney-General has taken us through the order of the learned District Judge dated 18.11.86, in which exception is taken to the statements made by the contemners in the applications under section 24; CPC and the deposition and the letter for taking up action against the contemners sent to the Registrar of this Court. The learned District Judge, in his above order, did not point out which statements of ; the contemners came within the mischief of contempt laws. Save and except saying that “দরখাস্তকারী অতি উৎসাহী হয়ে মুন্সেফের বিরুদ্ধে অত্যন্ত অবমাননাকর অভিযোগ আনয়ন করেছেন যার কোন ভিত্তি নেই।” 

 From the petition filed by contemner No. 1 under section 24 CPC as quoted above and also from the perusal of the other three similar petitions, it appears that the contemner No. 1 did not say in those petitions that the learned Munsif decided the above suits in favour of Azaharuddin "being influenced by him" although it is said in paragraph 3 of the petition that the learned Munsif decreed those suits, in spite of the fact that Azaharuddin could not prove his case. Thus, in our opinion the statements made by contemner No.1 Joynal Abedin in the four applications under section 24 CPC do not come within the mischief of Contempt of Court law. 

 9. In paragraph 3 of the supplementary affidavit submitted by contemner No. 1, it is stated that Mosharraf and Mokhatar Mia are also two nick-names of Mr. Lutfar Rahman, father-in-law of the learned Munsif concerned, Nobody denied this statement made by contemner No. 2 on oath. It may further be pointed that the learned Munsif concerned did not deny the statements made in the applications under section 24 CPC although, the learned District Judge called for a report from him by his order dated 3.8.85. In view of the above, it is clear that the statements of the contemners do not come within the mischief of the contempt laws. 

 10. It may be pointed out that in an application under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure, parties are to make grounds for seeking transfer of suits or cases from a particular court and in doing so, it is customary that certain allegations are made against the presiding officer which gave rise to apprehension in the minds of the litigants, that they would not get proper justice from a particular officer. The litigants are given certain latitude in such matters. It may be further pointed out that allegations against a presiding officer of the court should not be construed as contemptuous allegation to bring a court into disrepute or to lower the status and position of the Court in the eye of the public as the presiding officer of the court is not identical with the court itself. The court should not be touchy or sensitive with respect to the statements made against the presiding officers of the Court so as to start proceeding of the contempt in any and every case. In the present case it seems that the learned District Judge was not justified in referring the matter to this court for starting contempt proceeding on the ground stated in his order and in the letter of reference. In any view of the matter, we are of the opinion that no case for contempt is made out against any of the contemners in this case.
